chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ibn Maskan, from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Salih ibn Mitham narrated to me from Ubayyah al-Asadi that he heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying: By Allah, no servant ever hates me and dies with hatred for me but that he sees me at the moment of his death in a way that he hates (in a way that he hates), and no servant ever loves me and dies with love for me but that he sees me at the moment of his death in a way that he loves (in a way that he loves).' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is on his right side (on the right hand side).'

key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: at the moment of his death

ai.seo_question: What does a person see at the moment of death regarding the Prophet and Imams based on their love or hatred?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Kulayni’s contemporaries, establishes the concept of *al-Manzilah* (the abode/state) at the hour of death, where one’s eternal spiritual orientation is revealed through their vision of the Prophet and the Imams. Abu Ja'far al-Baqir confirms the report with a solemn oath, emphasizing that love (*mawaddah*) or hatred (*bukh*) for the Ahl al-Bayt dictates the quality of this final encounter, serving as a precursor to the Hereafter. This reflects the Shia theological principle that love for the Prophet's family is not merely emotional but a defining criterion of faith and salvation.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 3.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Yaḥyā al-Ḥalabī, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qaṣīr who said, “I said to Abā Jaʿfar (a), ‘Ṣāliḥ ibn Mītham narrated to me from ʿAbāyah al-Asadī that he heard ʿAlī (a) saying, “By Allah, no servant [of Allah] ever hates me and dies with hatred for me but that he sees me at the moment of his death in a way that he hates, and no servant ever loves me and dies with love for me but that he sees me at the time of his death in a way that he loves.”’ So Abū Jaʿfar (a) said, ‘Yes, and the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) will be on his right side.’”
